summary.short: Amends the Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018 and confers Secretary of State powers on the security and resilience of network and information systems used in essential activities. Extends duties to data centres, load controllers, managed service providers and critical suppliers, adds incident reporting, penalties and national-security directions.
summary.long: The Bill amends the Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018 (NIS Regulations) and gives the Secretary of State powers over the security and resilience of network and information systems used in essential activities. Part 2 extends the NIS Regulations to data centre services (a rated IT load of at least 1 megawatt, or 10 megawatts on an enterprise basis), to load controllers (potential electrical control of at least 300 megawatts) and to managed service providers. It adds registration, representative and incident-notification duties, customer notification, designation of critical suppliers, periodic cost-recovery charges, information-sharing rules, information notices and financial penalties. Part 3 lets the Secretary of State designate a statement of strategic priorities, make regulations on security and resilience (including requirements, enforcement, penalties and appeals), issue a code of practice, and report to Parliament at least every five years. Part 4 allows the Secretary of State to give national-security directions to regulated persons, with monitoring, information gathering, inspections, penalties and non-disclosure requirements. Part 5 sets the extent (England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland), the commencement (some provisions on the day of Royal Assent, some two months later, the rest by regulations) and the short title.

notes: Part 1 of 2: covers the Act's text from the contents and sections 1 to 61 up to the Schedules headings; the text of Schedules 1 and 2 is not in this part. The short title is the anticipated title (Cyber Security and Resilience (Network and Information Systems) Act 2026) while the bill is pending. Penalty maxima appear in several places with different figures: s.21 (NIS Regulations: £10,000,000 or 2% of turnover; £17,000,000 or 4%), s.32(3) (£17,000,000 or 10%), s.49(2) (£17,000,000 or 10%, or £10,000,000 for information duties) and s.52(5) (£10,000,000 for non-disclosure). The text does not state how these tiers relate beyond their stated application. The Information Commission is referred to as an existing body; its establishment is not set out in this part. Part 2 of 2 covers section 22 (enforcement and appeals) and Schedule 2 (minor and consequential amendments) as brought from the Commons. The NIS amendments are inserted, substituted or omitted text, not the consolidated regulations. Points to note: Schedule 2 paragraph 14 keeps regulations 2 and 3(6) in effect despite their revocation until the first statement is designated under section 25. Paragraph 6(1) names 'Regulation A20' as written in the text. Regulation 18(3A) and (3B) are referred to, but regulation 18 is not amended in this part. Regulation 16(8B)(a) excludes powers over premises outside the UK, while regulation 17(3ZA) allows enforcement steps outside the UK.
